inference.why_the_rounds_did_not_move: The ceiling counts revisions of the model and nothing about the model moved: the same reading, the same split, the same numbers. What moved is that a competing reading was knocked out from under it by a measurement, which is the opposite of a revision.

claim:
The phaser half of `11 08` is the phaser of `01 20`, rather than a second one built to the same description. The page prints the two types' first five parameters at the same five addresses, with the same five printed ranges, the same two conversion columns and the same five printed defaults. Two of those five were swept on the multi at exactly the settings the single type's records were taken at and under the hold those records were taken under, and the profiles are the same profiles. What separates two phasers is where they put their cancellations, and where a cancellation sits is a thing that moves when the byte moves -- so the difference between the two records is split into the part that depends on the setting and the part that does not, and only the first of them could be a difference between two blocks. Over the 97 bands this stimulus reaches, the part that depends on the setting is 0.041 dB at the median and 0.77 dB at its worst, against the 23.9 to 33.4 dB the byte itself commands over those same bands: 32 times under the smallest thing it does. A corner table that differed anywhere would have to hide inside that. The part that does not depend on the setting is 0.043 dB at the median, and it is not read here as a difference between the two phasers because the two chains are not the same chain: the single type carries a pair of tone controls at the centre of their range in the path and the multi carries none at that address at all. The largest raw differences in the whole comparison are not at the notches, where a reader would look for them -- they are at 39 Hz and below, in the 16 bands at the bottom of the set where the runs cannot tell one of their own takes from another by better than a decibel and a half. **And the type is two branches summed rather than two stages in series.** Each half carries its own level byte. With the wah half's at nothing the output stands 56.8 dB above this run's own silence against 57.5 dB with both halves up, and with the phaser half's at nothing what is left still stands 45.2 dB above it -- where two stages in series would leave nothing, whichever of the two bytes were the chain's own output level. A second pair was asked and came back neither way. The reading left standing here named a run -- the flanger's feedback byte on `02 0A` against `01 23`, a pair whose page renumbers the block two addresses down instead of lining it up -- and it was made. Where the two profiles agree they agree where a comb is decided: nine of the ten settings put teeth in the band set, and 89 of the single type's 101 teeth land in the same band as a tooth of the multi's -- at the two settings whose combs are shallowest and cleanest, every one of the eleven does, at 749, 1498, 2245, 2997, 3776, 4490, 5339 Hz and on up, so the delay line and the length it is set to are shared. Where they differ they differ by more than the phaser pair ever did: the part that depends on the setting is 0.187 dB at the median and 3.4 dB at its worst, against the 5.4 dB the byte commands at the weakest setting it actually does anything at -- a factor of two and a half where the phaser pair returned thirty-two. **And this run cannot say what the difference is.** Two of the single type's bytes have no counterpart on the multi: a pre filter, which its records held off and which this type does not have, and a phase byte, which its records held at nought and which nothing on this type reaches. A flanger run at a different fixed phase returns a comb in the same places and not the same depths, which is what is measured. So the reading that the machine builds a multi out of its blocks is supported where it can be checked and is not closed, and what would close it is a pair with nothing held that the multi cannot be asked to hold too.

Both halves of one multi reach their single types' blocks. The wah half was then asked the same way and answers the same way, which is the thing the first round listed first among what it did not settle. Its manual byte moves a band-pass across 1.83 octaves on both types, and the two put the peak in the same twelfth-octave band at eight of nine settings and one band apart at the ninth -- which is the closest a band reading can place two things. Where the stage found a width to fit a curve over, the two corners land between a thousandth and six hundredths of an octave apart. Split the same way the phaser was, the part of the difference that depends on the setting is a tenth of a decibel through the middle of the range and runs between eighteen and fifty times under what the byte commands at that same setting. Both halves of one multi are therefore the single types' blocks, reached at addresses neither type prints them at together, and the wah's are five higher than the wah's own.

A second multi reaches the same wah block. `11 06` puts an overdrive where `11 08` puts a phaser and prints the wah's seven parameters at the same seven addresses, and its corner lands where the other two land: eight of nine settings in the same twelfth-octave band as the single type, the ninth one band away, and where the stage found a width to fit a curve over, seven thousandths of an octave apart. Against the first multi it is seven of nine and three thousandths. The part of the difference that depends on the setting is 0.13 dB at the median and runs between thirteen and forty-two times under what the byte commands at that same setting. Three types therefore reach one auto wah, two of them multis assembled out of different pairs, and the block is the block rather than one type having been built out of the single ones.
named: one phaser and one auto wah, both reached from a type that is neither

document_rows.why: That the two types print five parameters that are the same five: the same offsets, the same ranges, the same defaults and the same conversion columns. That is what makes the question askable and it is not evidence that the answer is yes -- a page printing two tables alike is a fact about the page, and two blocks built alike would be printed exactly this way too. What the records add is that they measure the same.

That each half carries a level byte of its own, which is what makes the topology askable at all: a type with one output level could not be asked which of its halves is still there when the other is turned down.

era_priors.claim: A block that several types name is one routine reached with a parameter block, not a copy per type.
era_priors.why: The effects live in ROM and the machine offers sixty-five types built out of a much smaller set of named blocks. Copying a phaser into each of the dozen types that print one costs that block's code a dozen times over for nothing a listener could hear.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: A byte a page prints identically on a multi and on its single-effect sibling returned a different profile at the settings both were read at.

adds: The records say what each byte did to each band of each take on each of the two types, and what was left of the output with each half's level byte at nothing. What is read out of them here is that the two types' profiles are one profile to inside either run's own floor, and that the two halves are summed rather than chained. The records name no block, make no comparison between types, and say so.

alternatives.reading: Two implementations of a phaser that agree, rather than one reached from two places.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: Not applicable: the two readings differ in where the code is and in nothing that comes out of the sockets.
separated_by.why_not_separable: The same shape recorded twice in one archive. What the agreement does rule out is two *different* phasers, which is the thing that was worth asking: a corner table read at twenty-two settings and a resonance at three land within either run's own repeat scatter.
separated_by.why_it_was_separable_elsewhere: This reading was separable on another stage, and the reason it was is a property that stage has and this one does not. The equaliser's frequency table holds one entry that is not the third octave its printed range would give -- 279 Hz where the series says 315 -- and the two combination types carrying that section return it as well. Two implementations written from one printed range agree about what the range says; they do not agree about a constant neither could have read off it. The phaser's readings carry nothing of that kind: every figure the pair agrees about is a figure the page's own range and defaults would lead either implementation to. So the alternative is not separable here, and what would make it separable is a quantity on this pair that the page does not determine.

alternatives.reading: The agreement belongs to this pair rather than to how the machine builds a multi -- `11 08` was assembled out of the single types and the other eleven were not.

separated_by.observable: A block whose every byte the single type prints is printed on a multi too, with the same printed range and the same conversion column, swept on each at one set of settings under one hold, and the two readings laid over each other. What makes a pair answerable is that each side's reference sits inside its own sweep, so everything the swept byte does not reach divides out of both -- and what defeats one is a byte inside the block itself that only one type prints, because no reference removes that.

predicts.the machine builds a multi out of its bl: Profiles that agree to the floor, as these do.
predicts.this pair only: A profile that differs by more than either run's floor at some setting of the byte.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: One twelfth-octave band, which is where the two halves of `11 08` placed a moving band-pass at eight of nine settings and the closest a band reading can place anything. On the pair now queued the quantity is a rate rather than a place, and the rig repeats one to a few parts in a hundred thousand.

run.why:
The rotary's slow rate, on the multi that carries a rotary beside a phaser. Three things make it the best one left.

It is the largest block in the machine that a multi prints whole: ten parameters, against the phaser's five and the wah's seven, each with the same printed range and the same conversion column on both.

The renumbering is not a shift. `01 22` prints its ten at `03` through `0B` and then, after a gap at `0C`, at `0D`; `11 07` prints the same ten at `08` through `10` and then `11`, with no gap. Nine of them move five addresses and the tenth moves four. A multi that reached its sibling's block through a constant offset would be an address map that happens to line up, and this one cannot be.

It is read by a different stage. Both pairs asked so far were band profiles, so an agreement between them could in principle be something band profiles do rather than something the machine does. A rate is a frequency recovered from a modulation, measured in octaves and not decibels, and it cannot agree for that reason.

One sweep and not two: `01 22` is among the most measured types in this archive and its side of the comparison already exists, at this address, with the settle time recorded. The rotor accelerates, so the settle time is part of the reading and the multi's side has to copy it.

separated_by.what_the_run_returned: Made. The teeth agree band for band and the depths do not, by up to 3.4 dB against a byte that commands 5.4 dB at its weakest working setting. That supports the reading where it can be checked and does not close it, because this pair leaves two of the single type's bytes at values nothing on the multi reaches.

the_run_that_was_made_and_could_not_answ.why: Superseded by what this run found. A further pair is worth asking only if every byte behind the single type's record can be held on the multi as well, which is a property of the pair and not of the stage -- so the next one is chosen by reading the two parameter lists against each other before any hardware is booked.
the_run_that_was_made_and_could_not_answ.why_it_is_not_offered_again: Made, and it could not answer -- what it returned is in `what_the_second_pair_returned`. It is not offered again because the reason it could not answer is a property of the pair and not of the run: the single type prints a pre filter and a phase byte that the multi does not, so two of the bytes behind its record sat at values nothing on the multi reaches. Repeating it longer or finer would return the same thing.

the_run_that_was_made.why:
The auto wah's manual byte, which moves a filter's corner -- the one thing a band profile reads best and the one thing two blocks built separately are least likely to put in the same place. Swept on the single type and on the multi, where the page prints it five addresses up.

This pair can be held identically and that is why it is the one to make. Every byte the single type prints appears on the multi with the same printed range and the same hex range, so nothing behind either record sits at a value the other cannot be set to -- which is what stopped the flanger pair from answering. The wah's own sensitivity and depth go to nothing on both so that the filter stands still to be read.

On the multi the phaser half's level byte goes to nothing, which this claim already measures as leaving the wah half 45.2 dB above that run's own silence. Two branches summed is what makes that possible and it is measured here rather than assumed.

Two sweeps and not one: the single type carries no band record at this address, so its side has to be made too.
the_run_that_was_made.what_it_returned: In `what_the_third_pair_returned`. The two profiles agree, and the reason given here for choosing the pair was wrong -- see `the_rule_the_queue_was_using_was_wrong` in that section.

alternatives.ruled_out_by: A second multi, built out of a different pair, reaching the same block. `11 06` carries an overdrive beside the wah where `11 08` carries a phaser, and its corner lands in the same twelfth-octave band as the single type's at eight of nine settings, one band away at the ninth, with fitted corners seven thousandths of an octave apart. This alternative names `11 08` as the one type assembled out of the single ones, and `11 06` is one of the eleven it says were not. What it leaves is the six multis nobody has asked, which is a limit and is recorded as one in `what_this_does_not_settle`. Read in data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/11-06-0A-the-wahs-corner-on-a-second-multi-in-twelfths.json.

refuted_by: A byte the page prints identically on this multi and on the phaser returning a different profile at the settings both were read at, under the same hold and on the same band set. Or either half's level byte at nothing leaving silence, which would make the two stages a chain and make every profile here a reading of the two together.
could_have_been_refuted_by: The run that made it. Two profiles were laid over each other at every setting of two bytes, on a band set of a hundred and thirteen bands, with each run's own repeats giving the figure the difference had to get under. Nothing in the comparison was fitted and there was no free number in it.
what_this_does_not_settle: Which of the two halves is nearer the input, or whether either is. What the level bytes show is that neither half is in the other's path, which is what summed means; a sum has no order and the records cannot give one.
What the phaser's remaining three bytes do on the multi. Rate and depth were held at nothing so that the corner would stand still to be read, and the mix byte was the reference rather than a reading.

Whether the other ten types that put named blocks together reach their siblings' blocks. Two pairs have been asked. One agreed to inside both runs' own floors and the other agreed on the teeth and not on the depths, with two bytes it could not hold the same -- so what is established is that at least one multi is built this way and that a pair which cannot be held identically cannot answer the question however carefully it is run. Two more pairs have been asked since, in another family and on another stage: the mid section printed inside `04 01` and `04 03`, laid over the standalone equaliser's at the settings that type's own runs were read at. Both return its table, its five widths and its gain window. That is four pairs of the set, three of which agree everywhere they were asked, and it is still the three and not the set.

What differs between `02 0A`'s flanger and `01 23`'s. A phase byte nothing reaches, a pre filter this type does not print, and a second delay block in the path are all in the chain and none of them is separable from a different block by a band profile taken through all three.
What the wah's other six bytes do on either type. One byte of the seven was swept; the rest were held so that it could be read, and the filter type was asked at one of its two entries.

Whether the six multis nobody has laid over anything reach their siblings' blocks. The page prints nine types as two effects, at `11 00` through `11 08`. Three have been asked and all three answer: `11 08` on both of its halves, `11 07` on its low rotor above the transient, and `11 06` on its wah. What that is evidence of is the three, and the six are not a reading with a measurement behind it -- they are six pairs each choosable by the rule this claim now carries.

This type answers at `40 03 06` and `40 03 07`, resting at 1 and 0, and its pages print nothing at either. They were not written. Every profile is reported against a take of this same chain with the swept byte at its printed default, so whatever they do divides out of both sides as long as what they do does not depend on `40 03 0A` -- and that is not established here. It is the one byte-shaped hole left in this pair, and it is the same shape as the one that defeated the flanger pair, except that there the byte was inside the block being compared and here it is not.

what_the_second_pair_returned.what: The flanger's feedback byte read on `02 0A` at the settings and under the hold `01 23`'s record carries, and the two laid over each other the same way the phaser pair was. Reported as the teeth first and the decibels second, because on a comb the teeth are the thing a delay decides and the depths are what everything else does.
what_the_second_pair_returned.measured_in: Hz for the teeth, dB for the rest

the_setting_that_opens_the_loop.why_it_is_not_the_denominator: It is the byte at the centre of its printed range, which is no loop either way and is also the reference these profiles are reported against. Its span is what a flat profile's span is and dividing by it would make any difference look infinite.

what_the_second_pair_returned.what_this_run_holds_that_the_other_could: Nothing, and that is the finding. The phaser pair printed the same five parameters at the same five addresses, so every byte the single type's records held could be held here too. This pair does not: the single type prints a pre filter and a phase byte and the multi prints neither, so two of the seven bytes behind the record being compared against are at values on this type that nothing sets and no page states.
what_the_second_pair_returned.why_it_is_not_read_as_a_different_block: The teeth. A comb's teeth are where the delay puts them, and a different delay line, a different length or a different structure moves them. They did not move. What a phase byte at a different fixed value does is leave the teeth where they are and change how deep they are between the two channels, and how deep they are is what differs.
what_the_second_pair_returned.why_it_is_not_read_as_the_same_block_eit: The margin. Two and a half times under what the byte commands is not the thirty-two the phaser pair returned, and an explanation that fits is not a measurement that separates. Nothing here rules out a second flanger built to the same delay and a different summing.

how_many_teeth_land_in_the_same_band.why_not_all_of_them: The count is of local minima deeper than a decibel, taken band by band, so a shallow dip on one profile and not the other is counted as a tooth that did not match even where both combs are in the same place. The two settings whose combs are shallowest and cleanest match eleven for eleven with nothing over on either side; the settings with the deepest loop are where the counts part, and there the multi has more teeth than the single type rather than teeth elsewhere.

what_the_third_pair_returned.what: The wah's manual byte read on both types at nine settings, with the filter standing still -- sensitivity and depth at nothing on both, the filter set to band-pass on both, resonance left at the value the page prints as the default -- and the phaser branch of the multi switched off at its level byte. Each side is reported against a take of its own chain with the swept byte at its printed default, which is what makes the two comparable: no setting of this byte switches the filter out, and a reference taken inside the sweep removes everything the byte does not reach.
what_the_third_pair_returned.measured_in: octaves for where the feature sits, dB for the rest
what_the_third_pair_returned.why_the_place_is_the_reading_and_not_the: This byte moves a band-pass across 1.83 octaves, and a residual is nearly blind to a feature that moves sideways: sliding a peak costs a decibel or two on its flanks and nothing at its top. Where it sits is read off the same band set on both sides, so whatever a band-energy reading does to a peak it does to both.
what_the_third_pair_returned.why_the_worst_bands_are_where_they_are: Every setting's worst disagreement is between 111 and 445 Hz, at the bottom of what this stimulus reaches and below everything the band-pass passes. The two runs' own repeats of one setting scatter by 0.6 to 1.4 dB in those same bands, against a fifth of a decibel over the rest of the range. It was checked rather than assumed: each setting's worst band carries the two floors measured there.
what_the_third_pair_returned.the_rule_the_queue_was_using_was_wrong:
The rule this entry carried before the wah pair was made said that a pair is answerable when every byte the single type prints appears on the multi with the same printed range and the same hex range. Read against the pages that is false of the pair it was recommending: `01 21` prints a low and a high gain at `40 03 13` and `40 03 14` and `11 08` prints a level and a pan there, so the single type carries a tone control the multi has none of.

It is also the wrong rule, and the run shows why. Every profile in both sweeps is reported against a take of its own chain with the swept byte at one stated setting, so everything that does not depend on that byte divides out of both sides exactly -- a shelf pair at its centre and a run of static gains among them. What cannot divide out is a byte inside the block being compared, because it changes what the swept byte itself does. That is what the flanger pair's phase byte was.

Asked that way the question is about the block and not about the type: is every byte of the single type's own block printed on the multi with the same range? Twelve pairs in the machine answer yes, and the two largest of them have not been asked.

what_the_fourth_pair_returned.what: The same wah block on a second multi. `11 06` carries an overdrive where `11 08` carries a phaser, and prints the wah's seven at the same seven addresses `11 08` does. Swept at the same nine settings of the same byte, against a take of its own chain with that byte at the same printed default, on the same band set and read from the same channel.
what_the_fourth_pair_returned.measured_in: octaves for where the feature sits, dB for the rest
what_the_fourth_pair_returned.what_the_overdrive_branch_is: Summed with the wah rather than in front of it, which is what lets the branch be switched off at its level byte and is measured rather than assumed. With `40 03 13` at nothing the sweep's own reference takes sit 51.2 dB over this run's silence, which the record carries as `reference.above_the_silence_db`, so the wah reaches the output without the overdrive. The converse was taken as one take rather than a sweep -- the wah off at `40 03 15` and the overdrive at the 96 this unit rests it at -- and it came back 10.6 dB over the silence take and 1.7 dB under the wah's own, read as whole-take levels by the driver rather than as bands by the stage. It is in the takes manifest beside the question that asked for it and not in a record, because it carries no setting of the swept byte for a sweep to report it against. Nothing here rests on it: what the reading needs is that the wah reaches the output, and that is the record's own figure.
what_the_fourth_pair_returned.what_was_not_held: This type answers at `40 03 06` and `40 03 07`, resting at 1 and 0, and its pages print nothing at either. They were not written. Every profile is reported against a take of this same chain with the swept byte at its printed default, so whatever they do divides out of both sides as long as what they do does not depend on `40 03 0A` -- and that is not established here. It is the one byte-shaped hole left in this pair, and it is the same shape as the one that defeated the flanger pair, except that there the byte was inside the block being compared and here it is not.
what_the_fourth_pair_returned.why_the_worst_bands_are_where_they_are: As on the first pair, every setting's worst disagreement is between 105 and 297 Hz, below everything a band-pass at these settings passes. At those bands the two runs' own repeats of one setting scatter by 0.39 to 2.03 dB, which is the size of the disagreement itself -- so each setting carries the two floors measured at its own worst band rather than a figure taken from the middle of the range.
